purpose: libtiff is a library for reading, writing, and manipulating TIFF image files.

functions.TIFFComputeTile: `TIFFComputeTile` maps image coords `(x,y,z,s)` to a tile index. Use it to locate the tile containing a pixel/voxel in tiled TIFFs. It uses tile size, image size, and planar config; if sizes are invalid/0, result stays default/undefined-ish (`tile=1` then adjusted by omitted code).
functions.TIFFSwabDouble: `TIFFSwabDouble` byte-swaps a `double` in place (8 bytes). Use it on a valid `double*` when converting between opposite-endian data formats. It simply reverses the byte order; behavior is only defined for 8-byte doubles.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfLong8: Swaps byte order of an array of 64-bit values in place. Use it on `n` `uint64_t` elements when converting between host and opposite-endian TIFF data. `n<=0` does nothing; each element is byte-reversed.
functions.TIFFTileRowSize: Returns the byte size of one tile row. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` to size buffers or iterate tile data. It simply calls `TIFFTileRowSize64()` then casts to `tmsize_t`; if the value won’t fit, the cast helper handles the error/overflow case.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfShort: Swaps byte order of an array of 16-bit values in place. Use it on `uint16_t* wp` with count `n` to convert endianness. It processes each element sequentially; `n==0` does nothing. Requires `sizeof(uint16_t)==2`.
functions.TIFFNumberOfStrips: Returns the number of strip offsets for the current image. Use after TIFF directory is set. It computes strips from image length/RowsPerStrip, treating RowsPerStrip=-1 as 1 strip, and multiplies by SamplesPerPixel for PLANARCONFIG_SEPARATE.
functions.TIFFClose: `TIFFClose` closes a TIFF handle: it first runs `TIFFCleanup(tif)` to free internal TIFF resources, then calls the registered close procedure on the client file handle. Use it once you’re done with a `TIFF*`. It doesn’t return a status.
functions.TIFFForceStrileArrayWriting: Forces writing only the strile array (strip/tile offsets+bytecounts) to an already-written directory. Use only on writable TIFFs after the directory exists and when no other directory fields changed. Fails for read-only, unwritten, or DIRTYDIRECT cases.
functions.TIFFCIELabToXYZ: Converts CIE L*a*b* values to XYZ using the `TIFFCIELabToRGB` reference white (`X0,Y0,Z0`). Pass Lab inputs and valid float pointers for X/Y/Z. Low L uses the linear branch; otherwise cubic. No return value; outputs are written directly.
functions.TIFFSetFileno: `TIFFSetFileno` directly replaces a TIFF handle’s underlying file descriptor and returns the previous one. Use it only when you need to retarget an already-open `TIFF*` to another fd. It does no validation or I/O; it just assigns `tif_fd`.
functions.TIFFCleanup: `TIFFCleanup` finalizes a `TIFF*`: flushes pending data if not `O_RDONLY`, calls the format-specific cleanup, frees directory/client-info lists, and releases owned raw/mapped buffers. Use it when done with a TIFF handle; don’t use `tif` afterward.
functions.TIFFReadFromUserBuffer: `TIFFReadFromUserBuffer` reads a strile from a caller-supplied raw buffer instead of file I/O. Use it only on readable TIFFs and only when the compression scheme allows raw access; it sets TIFF to use your `inbuf`/`insize` as raw data, then decodes into `outbuf`. Returns 0 on error.
functions.TIFFIsByteSwapped: `TIFFIsByteSwapped()` checks a TIFF handle’s `TIFF_SWAB` flag and returns nonzero if the file’s data must be byte-swapped on this host, 0 otherwise. Use it to query endianness handling for an opened `TIFF*`; it doesn’t modify the object.
functions.TIFFGetSeekProc: `TIFFGetSeekProc` returns the current seek callback stored in a `TIFF*`. Use it to inspect which seek function libtiff will call for that handle. It doesn’t seek itself; it just returns `tif->tif_seekproc` (or whatever is currently set).
functions.TIFFScanlineSize: Returns the byte size of one image scanline. Use it to allocate/read a row buffer for a `TIFF*`. It calls `TIFFScanlineSize64()` then casts to `tmsize_t`; if the size can’t fit, the cast helper reports an error.
functions.TIFFGetClientInfo: `TIFFGetClientInfo` looks up a client-info entry by `name` in a TIFF handle and returns its stored `void*` data. Use it after client info has been attached to `tif`. If no matching name exists, it returns `NULL`.
functions.TIFFCurrentStrip: `TIFFCurrentStrip` returns the TIFF handle’s current strip index (`tif_curstrip`). Use it after setting/reading image data to query which strip the library is currently positioned on. It has no side effects and simply returns the stored value.
functions.TIFFFieldPassCount: `TIFFFieldPassCount` returns the `field_passcount` flag from a `TIFFField`. Use it to check whether that tag’s value count is stored/passed separately. It just reads the field; no validation or side effects.
functions.TIFFRasterScanlineSize: Returns the raster scanline byte size for a TIFF image. Use it to size buffers for one decoded row. It calls `TIFFRasterScanlineSize64()` then safely casts to `tmsize_t`; on overflow, the cast helper may signal failure/return an invalid size.
functions.TIFFReadRGBAImage: `TIFFReadRGBAImage` is a convenience wrapper that reads a TIFF into an RGBA raster using bottom-left orientation. Call it with the TIFF handle, target width/height, output pixel buffer, and `stop` flag. It simply forwards to `TIFFReadRGBAImageOriented(...)`.
functions.TIFFReverseBits: Reverses the bit order of each byte in a buffer in place using `TIFFBitRevTable`. Call with a valid `uint8_t*` and byte count `n`; it processes 8 bytes at a time, then any remainder. No-op if `n<=0`.
functions.TIFFFieldDataType: `TIFFFieldDataType` is a simple accessor: it returns the `field_type` stored in a `TIFFField`. Use it with a valid, non-NULL `TIFFField*`. It has no extra logic; behavior is just direct field retrieval, so invalid pointers will cause undefined behavior.
functions.TIFFFieldTag: `TIFFFieldTag` is a simple accessor that returns the TIFF tag number stored in a `TIFFField`. Use it with a valid, non-NULL `TIFFField*`. It does no checking or conversion; it just returns `fip->field_tag`.
functions.TIFFGetVersion: `TIFFGetVersion()` returns the library’s built-in version string (`TIFFVersion`). Use it to query libtiff’s version at runtime. It takes no args, has no side effects, and always returns the same const string pointer.
functions.TIFFIsBigEndian: `TIFFIsBigEndian(TIFF*)` checks a TIFF handle’s header magic to tell whether the file/object is big-endian. Use it on a valid `TIFF*`; it returns nonzero if `tiff_magic == TIFF_BIGENDIAN`, otherwise 0.
functions.TIFFReadRawStrip: `TIFFReadRawStrip` reads a strip’s **raw, uncompressed encoded bytes** into `buf`. Use a valid `strip` index and `size` as buffer capacity (or -1 to read full strip). Returns bytes read, or -1 on invalid strip, unsupported raw access, read check failure, or zero bytecount.
functions.TIFFFdOpen: `TIFFFdOpen` opens a TIFF stream from an existing file descriptor on Win32. Use it with a valid `fd`, filename label, and mode; it wraps `TIFFClientOpen` with std I/O callbacks. Returns `TIFF*` on success, `NULL` on failure; on success it stores `fd` in `tif->tif_fd`.
functions.TIFFIsMSB2LSB: `TIFFIsMSB2LSB()` checks whether a TIFF uses MSB-to-LSB bit fill order. Pass a valid `TIFF*`; it returns nonzero if `FillOrder == FILLORDER_MSB2LSB`, otherwise 0. Use it to test bit ordering before reading/writing packed data.
functions.TIFFSetClientInfo: Stores client-private data in a TIFF under a string key. Call with a TIFF handle, your data pointer, and a name; if the name exists it updates the data, otherwise it creates a new entry in the client-info list.
functions.TIFFGetTagListCount: `TIFFGetTagListCount(TIFF*)` returns the number of custom tag values currently stored in the TIFF directory (`td_customValueCount`). Use it to query how many custom tags are present; it just reads and returns that count, with no side effects.
functions.TIFFWriteCustomDirectory: `TIFFWriteCustomDirectory` is a thin wrapper to write a TIFF directory using `TIFFWriteDirectorySec` with both flags set to `FALSE`. Pass a valid `TIFF*` and `uint64_t*` to receive the directory offset. It returns the underlying write result.
functions.TIFFWriteCheck: `TIFFWriteCheck` validates that a TIFF is writable and that the write mode matches the image layout (tiles vs scanlines). Call it before writing data. It errors if opened read-only, layout mismatches, or required fields like `ImageWidth` aren’t set.
functions.TIFFGetWriteProc: `TIFFGetWriteProc` returns the current write callback stored in a `TIFF*`. Use it to inspect which function libtiff will call for output. It does no I/O and no validation; it simply returns `tif->tif_writeproc` (may be NULL if unset).
functions.TIFFSetWarningHandler: Sets libtiff’s global warning callback. Call it with a `TIFFErrorHandler` to replace the current handler; it returns the previous one. Passing `NULL` disables warning output. Affects all subsequent warnings process-wide.
functions._TIFFmemcpy: `_TIFFmemcpy` is a thin libtiff wrapper around `memcpy`. Use it to copy `c` bytes from `s` to `d`. It performs no extra checks or special handling; behavior is exactly `memcpy` with `tmsize_t` cast to `size_t`.
functions.TIFFRegisterCODEC: Registers a new TIFF compression codec in libtiff’s internal list. Use it with a scheme ID, codec name, and init callback; on success it returns the stored `TIFFCodec*`. If allocation fails, it logs an error and returns `NULL`.
functions.TIFFVTileSize: `TIFFVTileSize` returns the byte size of a tile covering `nrows` rows. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and row count to size tile buffers. It delegates to `TIFFVTileSize64` and casts to `tmsize_t`; overflow is handled by `_TIFFCastUInt64ToSSize`.
functions.TIFFSetWarningHandlerExt: Sets the global TIFF warning callback with an extended handler. Pass a `TIFFErrorHandlerExt` to install it; the previous handler is returned. If `handler` is `NULL`, warnings are effectively disabled until another handler is set.
functions.TIFFErrorExt: `TIFFErrorExt` reports a TIFF error via the registered handlers. Call it with a file handle, module name, and printf-style format. If `_TIFFerrorHandler` and/or `_TIFFerrorHandlerExt` are set, it invokes them; otherwise it does nothing.
functions.TIFFCurrentDirectory: Returns the current TIFF directory index stored in `tif->tif_curdir`. Use it after opening/navigating a TIFF to know which directory is active. It just reads and returns the value; no validation, side effects, or error handling.
functions.TIFFWriteEncodedStrip: Writes one encoded strip of image data. Use `strip`, `data`, `cc` after write checks; returns bytes written or `-1` on error. If `strip` exceeds current strips, it may grow strips, but not for `PLANARCONFIG_SEPARATE` (fails).
functions.TIFFComputeStrip: Computes the strip index for a given `row` and `sample` in the current TIFF directory. Use it to map image rows to strip numbers. For `PLANARCONFIG_SEPARATE`, it adds the sample’s image offset; if `sample` is out of range, it reports an error and returns 0.
functions.TIFFSetClientdata: `TIFFSetClientdata` sets `TIFF`’s client-data handle and returns the previous one. Use it to swap the per-`TIFF` user/context pointer. It always updates `tif->tif_clientdata`; the old value is returned, so callers can restore or save it.
functions.TIFFSetErrorHandler: `TIFFSetErrorHandler` sets the global libtiff error callback and returns the previous one. Use it to install your own handler (or restore the old/default by passing the saved handler). It affects subsequent error reporting globally.
functions.TIFFVStripSize: Returns the byte size of a strip for `nrows` rows. Use it to size/read/write strip data. It delegates to `TIFFVStripSize64()` then casts to `tmsize_t`; if the 64-bit size can’t fit, the cast handles the overflow case.
functions.TIFFGetBitRevTable: `TIFFGetBitRevTable(reversed)` returns a lookup table for byte bit-reversal. Use it when you need to choose between reversed and non-reversed byte mapping: nonzero `reversed` gives `TIFFBitRevTable`, zero gives `TIFFNoBitRevTable`.
functions.TIFFTileRowSize64: Returns the byte size of one tile row. Use it on a valid `TIFF*` with tile width/length set. It errors and returns 0 if tile width/length are 0, or if `SamplesPerPixel` is 0 for `PLANARCONFIG_CONTIG`.
functions.TIFFGetMapFileProc: `TIFFGetMapFileProc()` returns the current file-mapping callback stored in a `TIFF*`. Use it to query which `TIFFMapFileProc` libtiff will use for that handle. It just returns `tif->tif_mapproc`; if unset, it returns whatever is currently stored (possibly `NULL`).
functions.TIFFVStripSize64: `TIFFVStripSize64` computes the byte size of a strip for `nrows` rows (or full image if `nrows==(uint32_t)-1`). Use it with a valid `TIFF*`. It returns 0 on invalid YCbCr `SamplesPerPixel` or other size-calculation cases.
functions.TIFFCreateCustomDirectory:
Creates a new “custom” TIFF directory: resets to defaults, then installs the app-provided field definitions via `_TIFFSetupFields()`. Use it before writing/working with a nonstandard directory. It clears directory offsets/state; always returns 0.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. TIFFCreateCustomDirectory(tif, infoarray) requires infoarray to point to a valid TIFFFieldArray describing the custom directory fields. Do not pass NULL. Before calling, allocate or reference a properly initialized TIFFFieldArray with a valid fields pointer and count, and ensure the TIFF handle tif is successfully opened. Add a caller-side check such as if (tif != NULL && infoarray != NULL) TIFFCreateCustomDirectory(tif, infoarray); otherwise skip the call or fall back to standard directory creation APIs.
functions.TIFFIsTiled: `TIFFIsTiled` checks whether a TIFF image is stored in tiled layout. Use it on a valid `TIFF*` to choose tile-based vs scanline processing. It returns nonzero if tiled, 0 otherwise.
functions.TIFFGetUnmapFileProc: Returns the current file-unmap callback stored in the TIFF handle. Use it to query the function libtiff will call to unmap a mapped file. It just returns `tif->tif_unmapproc`; if none is set, it returns `NULL`.
functions.TIFFFileno: `TIFFFileno(TIFF*)` returns the underlying file descriptor stored in `tif->tif_fd`. Use it to access the OS-level fd for an open TIFF. It just returns the field value; behavior depends on the TIFF object state.
functions.TIFFCurrentRow: `TIFFCurrentRow(TIFF*)` is a simple accessor that returns the current row number stored in the TIFF handle. Use it on a valid `TIFF*` after/while reading or writing scanlines to query progress. It just returns `tif->tif_row`; no side effects or error handling.
functions.TIFFYCbCrtoRGB:
Converts one YCbCr pixel to RGB using precomputed tables in `TIFFYCbCrToRGB`. Use it with 8-bit Y, Cb, Cr values and valid output pointers. Inputs are clamped to 0..255; outputs are clamped to 0..255.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. TIFFYCbCrtoRGB() requires a properly initialized TIFFYCbCrToRGB conversion context before use. Do not pass a zeroed or stack-allocated struct directly after memset(). First initialize the TIFFYCbCrToRGB object with the appropriate libtiff setup routine that allocates and fills Y_tab, Cr_r_tab, Cb_g_tab, Cr_g_tab, and Cb_b_tab. Only call TIFFYCbCrtoRGB() after that initialization succeeds, and avoid calling it if the context pointers are NULL. Also ensure Y, Cb, and Cr are provided as expected 8-bit-range values, even though the function clamps them internally.
functions.uv_encode: Encodes CIE u′v′ chromaticity into a table index. Use it with valid `u,v` and rounding mode `em`. If `v`/`u` fall outside the supported grid, it falls back to `oog_encode(u,v)`; otherwise returns the encoded cell number.
functions.LogL10fromY: `LogL10fromY` converts a linear luminance `Y` to a 10-bit LogL code. Use it for LogL encoding. It clamps: `Y>=15.742`→`0x3ff`, `Y<=0.00024283`→`0`, otherwise returns `tiff_itrunc(64*(log2(Y)+12), em)`.
functions.TIFFVTileSize64: `TIFFVTileSize64` computes the byte size of a vertical tile strip for `nrows` rows, using 64-bit size. Use it after tile geometry is set. Returns 0 if tile dims are unset; special-cases packed YCbCr contig data with subsampling/round-up handling.
functions.TIFFGetReadProc: `TIFFGetReadProc` returns the current read callback (`tif_readproc`) stored in a `TIFF*`. Use it to inspect the active read procedure, not to read data. It simply returns that pointer; if `tif` is invalid, behavior follows the caller’s misuse.
functions.TIFFRGBAImageGet: `TIFFRGBAImageGet` is a thin dispatcher for reading an image into an RGBA raster. Use it only after `TIFFRGBAImage` is initialized with valid `get` and `put` handlers. If either is missing, it reports an error and returns 0; otherwise it calls `img->get(img, raster, w, h)` and returns that result.
functions.TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted: `TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted` gets a tag like `TIFFVGetField`, but if the tag isn’t explicitly set it returns the directory’s default value for known tags. Use it with a `va_list` and pointers for outputs. Returns 1 on success, 0 if tag unsupported.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfTriples: Swaps byte order of an array of 3-byte records (“triples”). Use with `tp` pointing to `n` consecutive triples. For each triple, byte 0 and 2 are exchanged; byte 1 stays unchanged. No-op if `n <= 0`.
functions.LogL10toY: Converts a 10-bit LogL code to luminance Y (linear light). Call with the LogL sample value; `0` maps to `0.0`. For nonzero values it returns `exp((ln2/64)*(p10+0.5) - ln2*12)`, i.e., the decoded luminance.
functions.TIFFIsCODECConfigured: Checks whether a TIFF compression codec is available/configured. Call with a codec scheme ID. Returns 1 only if `TIFFFindCODEC()` finds the codec and its `init` is set and not `NotConfigured`; otherwise returns 0.
functions.TIFFLastDirectory: `TIFFLastDirectory(TIFF*)` checks whether the current TIFF directory is the last one in the file. Use it on an open `TIFF*` to test `tif_nextdiroff`: returns nonzero if `tif_nextdiroff == 0`, otherwise 0. It does not modify the TIFF state.
functions.TIFFVSetField: `TIFFVSetField` is the varargs-backed setter used to assign a TIFF tag via a `va_list`. Call it with a valid `TIFF*`, tag ID, and matching arguments for that tag. It returns the tag handler result, or `0` if the tag can’t be changed.
functions.TIFFClientOpen: `TIFFClientOpen` opens a TIFF using caller-supplied I/O callbacks, not stdio/files. Pass a name, mode, clientdata, and read/write/seek/close/size/map/unmap funcs. It returns a `TIFF*` on success, or `NULL` on failure.
functions.TIFFGetStrileOffsetWithErr: Returns the offset for a given strile (strip/tile). Use with a valid `TIFF*`, strile index, and optional `pbErr` to detect failure. It delegates to the cached strip-offset entry; if unavailable/invalid, it signals error via `pbErr` and returns 0.
functions.TIFFCIELabToRGBInit: `TIFFCIELabToRGBInit` initializes a `TIFFCIELabToRGB` converter from a `TIFFDisplay` and optional reference white. It copies display params, precomputes lookup tables/steps for CIELab→RGB using the display gamma. Use it once before conversion; it returns `int` status.
functions.TIFFUnRegisterCODEC: Removes a previously registered codec from libtiff’s codec list. Call it with the exact `TIFFCodec*` passed to registration. If found, it unlinks and frees it; if not, it reports an error: “not registered.”
functions.TIFFRGBAImageBegin: `TIFFRGBAImageBegin` initializes a `TIFFRGBAImage` for RGBA raster access. Call it after opening a TIFF and before reading pixels; it validates the TIFF (`TIFFRGBAImageOK`), sets defaults, and prepares color maps/conversion state. Returns 0 on invalid input, else nonzero.
functions.LogL16toY: Converts a 16-bit LogL sample to luminance Y. Use it with a raw `int` pixel value. If the low 15 bits are 0, it returns 0. Otherwise it computes `exp(...)`; the sign bit (`0x8000`) makes the result negative.
functions.TIFFNumberOfTiles: Returns the total tile count for the current TIFF image. Use after tags are set; it uses image/tile dimensions, falls back to full image size if tile size is unset, returns 0 if any tile dim is 0, and multiplies by samples/pixel for PLANARCONFIG_SEPARATE.
functions.TIFFCheckTile: `TIFFCheckTile` validates tile coordinates `(x,y,z,s)` against the TIFF image bounds. Use it before tile access; it returns 1 if valid, 0 if out of range and emits an error via `TIFFErrorExt`.
functions.TIFFRGBAImageEnd: `TIFFRGBAImageEnd` is cleanup/destructor for `TIFFRGBAImage`. Call it after RGBA image use to free internal lookup tables/buffers (Map, BWmap, PALmap, ycbcr, etc.) and NULL them. Safe to call when fields are already NULL; it just skips them.
functions.TIFFReadScanline: `TIFFReadScanline` reads/decompresses one image row into `buf`. Use it after opening a TIFF for reading, passing the target `row` and `sample`. It returns `1` on success, `-1` on error. If the row is already positioned, it decodes that row and advances to the next.
functions.TIFFReadRGBATile: `TIFFReadRGBATile` is a convenience wrapper for reading one tile as RGBA pixels. Call it with a TIFF handle, tile origin (`col`,`row`), and an output raster buffer. It simply forwards to `TIFFReadRGBATileExt(..., 0)`, so behavior is defined by that routine.
functions.TIFFSetupStrips: `TIFFSetupStrips` initializes strip/tile bookkeeping for a TIFF: computes strips-per-image and total strips, checks size limits, then allocates `StripOffsets`/`StripByteCounts` arrays. Call it during directory setup before writing/using strip data. Fails on oversized or alloc errors.
functions.TIFFGetStrileByteCountWithErr: Returns the byte count for a given strile (strip/tile), using the cached StripByteCounts entry. Call with a valid `TIFF*` and strile index; `pbErr` gets set on failure. It just forwards to the internal lookup helper.
functions.TIFFReadRGBAStripExt: Purpose: read one full strip into an RGBA raster. Use only on non-tiled TIFFs, with `row` at the strip start (`row % RowsPerStrip == 0`). It returns 0 on error; `stop_on_error` controls whether decoding stops on the first error.
functions.TIFFSetDirectory: Seeks to directory `dirn` in a TIFF by walking the IFD chain, then reads it. Use with a valid `TIFF*` and 0-based directory index. Returns 0 on failure/EOF; on success loads that directory and updates current/next dir state.
functions.TIFFSetSubDirectory: `TIFFSetSubDirectory` sets the next IFD offset, resets the directory counter/seen-list to avoid IFD loops, then calls `TIFFReadDirectory`. Use it to jump to a specific subdirectory. It returns `TIFFReadDirectory`’s result, so success/failure depends on reading that directory.
functions.TIFFFieldWriteCount: `TIFFFieldWriteCount` is a simple accessor for a `TIFFField`’s `field_writecount`. Use it to query how many values a tag expects when being written. It just returns the stored count; no validation or special-case handling.
functions.TIFFSwabLong: `TIFFSwabLong` byte-swaps a 32-bit `uint32_t` in place. Pass a valid pointer to one 4-byte value; it reverses the 4 bytes to convert between endiannesses. It assumes `sizeof(uint32_t)==4` and has no return value.
functions.TIFFPrintDirectory: `TIFFPrintDirectory` is a debug/diagnostic helper that prints the current TIFF directory fields to a `FILE*`. Call it with a valid `TIFF*`, output stream, and flags; it only reports metadata and handles whichever fields are set.
functions.TIFFCheckpointDirectory: `TIFFCheckpointDirectory` writes the current directory as a checkpoint while keeping the file open for more data. Use it during incremental writing. It ensures strip arrays are set up, writes the directory, then seeks to EOF and updates the write offset.
functions.TIFFCreateGPSDirectory: `TIFFCreateGPSDirectory` creates a GPS IFD using libtiff’s built-in GPS field set. Call it with a valid `TIFF*` before writing GPS tags. It simply fetches GPS fields and delegates to `TIFFCreateCustomDirectory`; it returns that result.
functions.TIFFGetFieldDefaulted: Returns a tag value like `TIFFGetField`, but supplies default values for missing tags. Call with `TIFF*`, tag, and output pointers. It forwards to `TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted`; returns success/failure.
functions.TIFFGetTagListEntry: `TIFFGetTagListEntry` returns the tag ID at `tag_index` from a TIFF’s custom tag list. Use it to iterate valid custom tags in `0..td_customValueCount-1`. If `tag_index` is out of range, it returns `(uint32_t)-1`.
functions.TIFFReadEncodedStrip: `TIFFReadEncodedStrip` reads and decodes one strip into `buf`. Use it with a valid `TIFF*`, strip index, and buffer size. It returns decoded bytes or `-1` on error. For uncompressed strips, it may fast-path via raw read + bit-reversal/postdecode.
functions.TIFFYCbCrToRGBInit:
Initializes a `TIFFYCbCrToRGB` conversion table for YCbCr→RGB. Pass the struct plus luma and refBlackWhite arrays. It precomputes clamp/lookup tables; if inputs are invalid, behavior depends on the caller—no extra validation shown.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Do not pass a standalone stack-allocated TIFFYCbCrToRGB object to TIFFYCbCrToRGBInit(). The function expects ycbcr to point to a buffer large enough to hold the TIFFYCbCrToRGB struct plus its trailing lookup tables, because it computes internal table pointers from memory immediately following the struct. Allocate a sufficiently large heap buffer (or use the library's expected allocation pattern) covering sizeof(TIFFYCbCrToRGB) plus the extra table storage, zero-initialize it if needed, then cast/use it as TIFFYCbCrToRGB*. Also ensure luma points to at least 3 valid floats and refBlackWhite to at least 6 valid floats.
functions.LogLuv32toXYZ: Decodes a packed 32-bit LogLuv pixel into CIE XYZ. Use it by passing the encoded `uint32_t` and a 3-float output array. If luminance decodes to `<= 0`, it returns `XYZ={0,0,0}`; otherwise it computes XYZ from the stored L,u,v values.
functions.TIFFSetErrorHandlerExt: Sets the global extended TIFF error callback. Pass a `TIFFErrorHandlerExt` to install it; the function returns the previous handler. It just swaps `_TIFFerrorHandlerExt`, so `NULL` disables the ext handler.
functions.TIFFTileSize64: `TIFFTileSize64` returns the byte size of one tile as a 64-bit value. Use it on a valid `TIFF*` after tile layout is set. It simply delegates to `TIFFVTileSize64(tif, td_tilelength)`, so behavior depends on the current directory/tile settings.
functions.TIFFReadRGBATileExt: `TIFFReadRGBATileExt` reads a single tile into an RGBA raster. Use it only on tiled TIFFs, and `col,row` must be the tile’s top-left corner. It returns 0 on invalid use/error; `stop_on_error` controls whether read errors abort or continue.
functions.TIFFGetCloseProc: `TIFFGetCloseProc` returns the close callback stored in a `TIFF*` handle. Use it to inspect the current close routine. It does no validation or side effects; it simply returns `tif->tif_closeproc` (or whatever is currently set).
functions.TIFFAccessTagMethods: `TIFFAccessTagMethods()` returns a pointer to the `TIFF` handle’s internal `TIFFTagMethods` table. Use it to inspect or modify tag-method callbacks for that `TIFF` object. It does no validation or copying; it simply returns `&tif->tif_tagmethods`.
functions.TIFFGetSizeProc: `TIFFGetSizeProc(TIFF*)` returns the `TIFFSizeProc` callback stored in the `TIFF` handle. Use it to query the current size-procedure function pointer. It doesn’t compute anything itself; it just returns `tif->tif_sizeproc` from that object.
functions.uv_decode: `uv_decode` maps a valid `(u',v')` index `c` to the center coordinates `*up`, `*vp`. Use it with `0 <= c < UV_NDIVS`; it returns `0` on success, `-1` if out of range. It binary-searches the row table to decode the index.
functions.TIFFFindCODEC: `TIFFFindCODEC` looks up a codec by compression scheme ID. Use it to query whether a codec is registered/builtin and get its `TIFFCodec*`. It searches registered codecs first, then builtin ones; returns `NULL` if no match.
functions.TIFFRawStripSize: Returns the raw byte size of a given strip, delegating to `TIFFRawStripSize64`. Use it to size/read compressed strip data. If the 64-bit result is `-1`, it returns `-1`; if it overflows `tmsize_t`, it reports “Integer overflow” and returns `0`.
functions.TIFFSetTagExtender: `TIFFSetTagExtender` sets libtiff’s global tag-extension callback used to register custom TIFF tags. Call it once to install your `TIFFExtendProc`; it returns the previous extender so you can chain/restore it. Passing `NULL` disables the hook.
functions.TIFFCurrentTile: `TIFFCurrentTile` returns the current tile index stored in the `TIFF` handle (`tif->tif_curtile`). Use it after tile-based operations to query which tile is currently selected/being processed. It just returns that value; no extra logic or validation.
functions.TIFFRasterScanlineSize64: Computes the raster scanline size in bytes for the current TIFF directory, using 64-bit math. Use after TIFF setup to size buffers. Contig: width*bits/sample*spp, then round up to bytes. Separate: round width*bits/sample to bytes, then multiply by spp.
functions.TIFFOpen: `TIFFOpen(name, mode)` opens a TIFF file by pathname. It validates `mode`, opens the file descriptor (`O_BINARY` if needed), then wraps it with `TIFFFdOpen`. On invalid mode or open failure, it returns `NULL` and reports an error; if `TIFFFdOpen` fails, it closes the fd.
functions.TIFFNumberOfDirectories: Counts TIFF directories by following the IFD chain from the header. Use it to query how many directories exist in the file. Returns a `uint16_t`; on overflow it logs an error and returns `65535`. If no directories, returns `0`.
functions._TIFFmemset:
`_TIFFmemset` is a thin libtiff wrapper over `memset`. Use it to fill `c` bytes at `p` with byte value `v` (converted to `size_t`). It has no extra checks or special behavior; it just forwards to `memset`.
Not directly misused by the caller. _TIFFmemset() crashes only because TIFFYCbCrToRGBInit() passes it an out-of-bounds pointer derived from an undersized ycbcr buffer. Prevent the crash by fixing the TIFFYCbCrToRGBInit() call as described above.
functions.TIFFSetFileName: `TIFFSetFileName` sets `tif->tif_name` to the given string and returns the previous name. It’s a simple metadata setter, not a copy: the caller must keep `name` valid for the TIFF object’s lifetime. If `name` is `NULL`, it stores `NULL` and returns the old value.
functions.TIFFSwabShort: `TIFFSwabShort` swaps the two bytes of a 16-bit `uint16_t` in place. Use it on a valid pointer to one short; it’s meant for byte-order conversion. It assumes `sizeof(uint16_t)==2` and always swaps the value.
functions.TIFFFieldWithTag: Returns the `TIFFField` metadata for a tag in a `TIFF*`. Use it to query a tag’s definition. It calls `TIFFFindField(..., TIFF_ANY)`; if the tag is unknown, it logs an internal error and returns `NULL`.
functions.TIFFReadRGBAImageOriented: Reads a TIFF into an RGBA raster with a requested orientation. Call after allocating `rwidth*rheight` pixels; it writes the image at `raster + (rheight-img.height)*rwidth`. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure; errors are reported via `TIFFErrorExt`.
functions.TIFFWriteScanline: `TIFFWriteScanline` writes one image row to a TIFF. Use it with a valid `TIFF*`, a row buffer, row index, and sample index. It checks write/strip state and buffer setup, may extend `ImageLength` for contiguous data, but fails for separate planes if the row exceeds current length.
functions.TIFFFieldReadCount: `TIFFFieldReadCount` returns a TIFF field’s stored read-count metadata (`field_readcount`). Use it to inspect how many values a tag expects when reading TIFF fields. It’s a simple accessor: no validation, no side effects, and it just returns the value in the `TIFFField` struct.
functions.TIFFReadCustomDirectory: Design: read a TIFF directory using a caller-supplied field table (`infoarray`) instead of the built-in tags. Use it after opening a TIFF and before accessing that custom IFD. It cleans prior state, loads the directory at `diroff`, and returns 0 on fetch/error; unknown tags are warned about and may be skipped.
functions.TIFFVGetField: `TIFFVGetField` is the varargs core for reading a tag’s value(s) from a TIFF. Use it with a `va_list` for a known tag. It returns the tag handler result if the tag exists and is set (or is a pseudo-tag); otherwise it returns 0.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfFloat: Swaps byte order of an array of `float` in place. Use it on `n` 4-byte floats when converting between opposite-endian data. It loops over each element, swapping bytes 0↔3 and 1↔2; `n==0` does nothing.
functions.TIFFScanlineSize64: Returns the 64-bit byte size of one image scanline. Use it to allocate/read/write row buffers. For contiguous YCbCr with 3 samples and no upsampling, it applies subsampling rules; invalid sample/subsampling values trigger an error and return 0.
functions.TIFFError: `TIFFError` reports a libtiff error via the registered error handlers. Call it with a module name and printf-style format string. If `_TIFFerrorHandler` and/or `_TIFFerrorHandlerExt` are set, both are invoked; if neither is set, it does nothing.
functions.TIFFSetMode: `TIFFSetMode` simply sets `tif->tif_mode` to the given `mode` and returns the previous mode. Use it to change a TIFF handle’s mode and keep the old value if you need to restore it. No validation or side effects beyond assignment.
functions.LogLuv24fromXYZ: Encodes an XYZ color into a 24-bit LogLuv value: luminance via `LogL10fromY`, chroma via `uv_encode`, then packs as `(Le<<14)|Ce`. Pass `XYZ[3]` and exposure `em`. If Y is invalid/zero or `s<=0`, it uses neutral u,v; `Ce<0` falls back to neutral.
functions.TIFFCurrentDirOffset: `TIFFCurrentDirOffset` returns the current TIFF directory’s file offset (`tif_diroff`). Use it after a directory is selected/read to know where that IFD is located in the file. It simply returns the stored offset; no I/O or validation.
functions.TIFFReadEncodedTile: Reads one tile in decoded form into `buf`. Use `tile` index and a buffer at least `size` bytes. Returns bytes read or -1 on error. Fast-path: uncompressed, enough space, not mapped, no raw-read禁制; then reads raw tile, bit-reverses if needed, and post-decodes.
functions.TIFFReadEXIFDirectory: `TIFFReadEXIFDirectory` loads an EXIF IFD from offset `diroff` into a `TIFF*` using libtiff’s EXIF field definitions. Call it with a valid TIFF handle and EXIF directory offset. It returns `TIFFReadCustomDirectory`’s result: success/failure.
functions.LogL16fromY: Converts a luminance `Y` to a 16-bit LogL value. Use it for positive/negative Y; `em` controls truncation via `tiff_itrunc`. Large `Y` clamps to `0x7fff`/`0xffff`, near zero returns `0`, and negative `Y` maps to signed LogL form.
functions.TIFFCreateEXIFDirectory: `TIFFCreateEXIFDirectory` creates a new TIFF directory using the EXIF tag set. Call it on a valid `TIFF*` before writing EXIF metadata. It returns the result of `TIFFCreateCustomDirectory`; success/failure depends on that call.
functions.TIFFWarningExt: `TIFFWarningExt` emits a libtiff warning with an extra client handle `fd`. Call it with a module name and printf-style format. If set, it invokes `_TIFFwarningHandler` and `_TIFFwarningHandlerExt`; if neither is installed, it does nothing.
functions.TIFFWriteBufferSetup: `TIFFWriteBufferSetup` sets the TIFF write/raw output buffer. Pass your own buffer `bp,size`, or `size=-1` to let libtiff allocate a buffer sized to strip/tile data (+10%, min 8KB). If `tif->tif_rawdata` existed, it’s freed if owned. On malloc failure it reports “No space for output buffer”.
functions.TIFFGetMode: `TIFFGetMode(TIFF*)` is a simple accessor that returns the TIFF handle’s current open mode (`tif_mode`). Use it on a valid `TIFF*` to query how the file was opened. It just returns the stored mode; no validation or side effects.
functions.TIFFGetConfiguredCODECs: Returns a heap-allocated array of configured codecs. Use it to enumerate registered + built-in codecs that are enabled. It grows via realloc, copies each `TIFFCodec`, and returns `NULL` on allocation failure. Free with `_TIFFfree()`.
functions.TIFFReadDirectory: `TIFFReadDirectory` advances to the next IFD, fetches/parses it, updates `tif->tif_curdir`/offsets, and cleans prior codec state. Use it after setting `tif_nextdiroff` to move through directories. Returns 0 on EOF/bad/looped offset or read failure; otherwise nonzero.
functions.TIFFReadRawTile: Reads a tile’s *raw/compressed* bytes into `buf`. Use with a valid `tile` index and `size` as buffer capacity; `-1` means “read full tile”. Returns bytes read, or `-1` on error/out-of-range/unsupported raw access.
functions.TIFFReadTile: `TIFFReadTile` reads and decodes one tile into `buf`. Call it with valid tile coords `(x,y,z,s)`; it first checks read mode and tile bounds. On failure it returns `-1`, otherwise it reads the encoded tile via `TIFFReadEncodedTile`.
functions.TIFFFlush: `TIFFFlush` writes pending image data/metadata to disk. Use it after modifying a TIFF opened non-readonly. In `O_RDONLY` it returns 1 and does nothing. It first flushes data, then may rewrite only strip/tile maps in `r+`, else rewrites the directory; failures return 0.
functions.TIFFIsUpSampled: `TIFFIsUpSampled(TIFF*)` is a simple query API that reports whether a TIFF handle is using upsampled sample data. Call it with a valid `TIFF*`; it returns nonzero if upsampling is enabled, 0 otherwise. It just forwards to `isUpSampled(tif)`.
functions.TIFFDataWidth: `TIFFDataWidth` maps a `TIFFDataType` to its byte size for tag/data handling. Use it to size buffers or compute storage. Returns 1, 2, 4, or 8 for known types; 0 for unknown/unsupported types (and `case 0`).
functions.TIFFXYZToRGB: `TIFFXYZToRGB` converts CIE XYZ values to RGB using the `TIFFCIELabToRGB` conversion tables/matrix. Use it with a prepared `cielab` context and output pointers for R/G/B. It clips inputs to valid ranges, bounds indices, and returns rounded 32-bit channel values.
functions.TIFFGetField: `TIFFGetField` is a varargs wrapper for `TIFFVGetField`, used to read a tag’s value(s) from a `TIFF*`. Call it with the tag and pointers for outputs. It returns the status from `TIFFVGetField` (success/failure).
functions.TIFFWriteTile: `TIFFWriteTile` writes one tile of image data at `(x,y,z,s)`. It first validates the tile coords with `TIFFCheckTile`; on failure it returns `-1`. Otherwise it computes the tile index and calls `TIFFWriteEncodedTile`, passing `-1` size so libtiff clamps to the tile size automatically.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfDouble: Swaps byte order of an array of `double` values in place. Use it on `n` doubles when TIFF data endianness differs from host. If `n<=0`, it does nothing; assumes `sizeof(double)==8`.
functions.TIFFReadBufferSetup: Sets the read buffer for a TIFF. Use `bp,size` to supply your own buffer, or `bp=NULL` to let libtiff allocate/zero one (rounded up). It frees any prior owned buffer. Returns 0 on invalid size/allocation failure.
functions.TIFFSetWriteOffset: `TIFFSetWriteOffset` simply sets `tif->tif_curoff` to the given file offset. It’s used to tell libtiff where the next write should start. No validation or extra logic: it just assigns the value.
functions.TIFFReadGPSDirectory: `TIFFReadGPSDirectory` reads a GPS IFD at `diroff` into `tif` using the GPS field definitions. Use it when you know the GPS directory offset. It just delegates to `TIFFReadCustomDirectory`; success/failure is its return value.
functions.TIFFStripSize: `TIFFStripSize` returns the byte size of one strip for a TIFF image. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` to size strip buffers or I/O. It calls `TIFFStripSize64` then casts to `tmsize_t`; if the 64-bit size won’t fit, the cast helper handles it.
functions._TIFFmemcmp: `_TIFFmemcmp` is a thin wrapper around `memcmp` for libtiff. Use it to compare `c` bytes from `p1` and `p2`. It returns `<0`, `0`, or `>0` like `memcmp`. `c` is cast to `size_t`; behavior is otherwise identical.
functions.LogLuv32fromXYZ: Encodes XYZ to a 32-bit LogLuv pixel: 16-bit log luminance in high bits, 8-bit u/v chroma in low bits. Use with XYZ[3] and em scaling. If Y is 0/invalid or s<=0, it falls back to neutral u,v; u/v are clamped to 0..255.
functions.XYZtoRGB24: Converts XYZ floats to 24-bit RGB using CCIR-709 primaries and ~2.0 gamma. Call with `xyz[3]` input and `rgb[3]` output. Each channel is clamped: `<=0→0`, `>=1→255`, else `256*sqrt(v)` cast to `uint8_t`.
functions.TIFFClientdata: `TIFFClientdata(TIFF*)` returns the client-supplied handle (`thandle_t`) stored in a `TIFF` object. Use it to retrieve the opaque I/O/context pointer passed when the TIFF was opened. It just returns `tif->tif_clientdata`; no extra logic or error handling.
functions.TIFFWriteRawTile: Writes raw, already-encoded tile data directly to a TIFF tile. Use only for tiled output; `tile` must be in range or it returns -1. On success it appends `cc` bytes and returns `cc`; otherwise -1.
functions._TIFFmalloc:
`_TIFFmalloc` is a thin TIFF wrapper around `malloc`. Use it to allocate `s` bytes for libtiff-related memory. If `s == 0`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns `malloc(s)`’s result, including possible allocation failure (`NULL`).
Use _TIFFmalloc only for positive allocation sizes and treat a 0-size request as producing no allocation. Initialize the pointer to NULL when size is 0, and ensure later cleanup code tolerates NULL without attempting to free stale pointers from prior allocations.
functions.TIFFFieldWithName: Returns the `TIFFField` for a tag name. Use it to look up metadata by name on a `TIFF*`. It calls `_TIFFFindFieldByName(..., TIFF_ANY)`; if not found, it reports an internal error and returns `NULL`.
functions.TIFFFreeDirectory: `TIFFFreeDirectory` frees/reset the in-memory `TIFFDirectory` state for a `TIFF*`: clears field-set bits, releases allocated tag/value buffers and custom tag values. Use it when discarding a directory or before reusing/closing the handle; it doesn’t read/write file data.
functions.TIFFStripSize64: `TIFFStripSize64` returns the byte size of one strip for a TIFF image. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` to size strip buffers or estimate I/O. It clamps rows-per-strip to image length, then delegates to `TIFFVStripSize64`; if rows/length are small, it returns the corresponding strip size.
functions.TIFFTileSize: `TIFFTileSize` returns the byte size of one tile for a TIFF image. It calls `TIFFTileSize64()` then safely casts to `tmsize_t`. Use it when you need the tile buffer size; if the size can’t fit in `tmsize_t`, the cast helper handles the error/overflow case.
functions.TIFFWarning: `TIFFWarning` reports a non-fatal warning. Call it with a module name and `printf`-style format string; it forwards the message to the installed warning handler(s). If no handler is set, it does nothing.
functions.TIFFDefaultStripSize: `TIFFDefaultStripSize` is a thin wrapper that delegates to the TIFF object’s `tif_defstripsize` method. Use it to get the library’s default strip size for a given `request`. Behavior depends entirely on the TIFF instance’s installed handler; it just forwards the call.
functions.TIFFGetStrileOffset: Returns the byte offset of a strile (strip/tile) in a TIFF. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and strile index. It’s a thin wrapper over `TIFFGetStrileOffsetWithErr(..., NULL)`, so it just returns the offset and does not report errors itself.
functions.TIFFWriteDirectory: `TIFFWriteDirectory` is a convenience wrapper to write the current TIFF directory/IFD. Call it after setting tags and image data for the current page. It delegates to `TIFFWriteDirectorySec(tif, TRUE, TRUE, NULL)` and returns that result.
functions._TIFFfree:
`_TIFFfree` is a thin wrapper around `free()`. It’s meant to release heap memory allocated by libtiff/internal allocators. Call it with a pointer previously allocated on the heap; passing `NULL` is safe, and freeing invalid/non-heap pointers is undefined.
Only call _TIFFfree on pointers that are currently owned and not already released. After any successful _TIFFfree, set the pointer to NULL. Also set the pointer to NULL after _TIFFrealloc(ptr, 0), because that call may already free the memory.
functions.TIFFFileName: `TIFFFileName(TIFF*)` returns the file name string stored in the `TIFF` handle (`tif->tif_name`). Use it to query the associated TIFF object's name for logging/debugging. It just returns the pointer; no validation or copying.
functions.TIFFSwabFloat: `TIFFSwabFloat` byte-swaps a 4-byte `float` in place, converting between little- and big-endian layouts. Pass a valid `float*`; it directly mutates the value. It assumes `sizeof(float)==4` and is only safe for 4-byte floats.
functions.TIFFReadRGBAStrip: `TIFFReadRGBAStrip` is a thin wrapper for `TIFFReadRGBAStripExt(..., 0)`. It reads one TIFF strip into an RGBA raster starting at `row`. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and output buffer; it returns the underlying function’s status.
functions.TIFFGetStrileByteCount: Returns the byte count for a given strile (strip/tile). Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and strile index. It’s a thin wrapper around `TIFFGetStrileByteCountWithErr(..., NULL)`, so it just returns the count and does no explicit error reporting here.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfLong: `TIFFSwabArrayOfLong` byte-swaps an array of 32-bit `uint32_t` values in place, converting endianness. Use it on `lp` with `n` elements. It always swaps each item; `n==0` does nothing.
functions.TIFFSetField: `TIFFSetField` is a varargs wrapper to set a TIFF tag/value on a `TIFF*`. Call it as `TIFFSetField(tif, tag, value...)`; it forwards args to `TIFFVSetField`. It returns that function’s status, so success/failure depends on the tag and supplied values.
functions.TIFFUnsetField: `TIFFUnsetField` clears a TIFF tag from the current directory. Use it with a tag ID to remove a set field. It returns 0 if the tag isn’t known; built-in tags clear their bit, custom tags free stored value and remove it from `td_customValues`.
functions.TIFFMergeFieldInfo: `TIFFMergeFieldInfo` adds `n` custom `TIFFFieldInfo` entries to a `TIFF*`’s field table. Use it after opening a TIFF to register extra tags/fields. It allocates/grows `tif_fieldscompat`; on allocation failure it reports an error and returns `-1`.
functions.TIFFFieldName: `TIFFFieldName` is a simple accessor for a `TIFFField`’s name. Pass a valid `TIFFField*`; it returns `field_name` as a `const char*`. It does no validation or allocation, and behavior is undefined if `fip` is null or invalid.
functions.TIFFRewriteDirectory: `TIFFRewriteDirectory` rewrites the current directory in-place when possible. If the directory was never written, it just calls `TIFFWriteDirectory`. Otherwise it clears the old directory link/header pointer, then relinks and writes the updated directory. On write/header errors, it returns 0.
functions.TIFFDeferStrileArrayWriting: Sets `td_deferstrilearraywriting` to defer writing strile arrays. Call it only before the first directory is written, and not on read-only TIFFs. Returns 1 on success, 0 with an error if mode is `O_RDONLY` or the directory was already written.
functions._TIFFrealloc:
`_TIFFrealloc` is a thin libtiff wrapper around `realloc()`. Use it to resize a heap block previously allocated by compatible allocators; pass `NULL` to allocate, or an existing pointer to grow/shrink. On failure it returns `NULL` and leaves the original block unchanged.
Yes, this is API misuse. Do not assume a NULL return means the original pointer is still valid when calling _TIFFrealloc(p, 0). Since _TIFFrealloc wraps realloc(), a size of 0 may free p and return NULL. To avoid double-free, handle zero-size realloc explicitly: if new_size == 0, call _TIFFfree(p); set p = NULL; and do not free it again later. For nonzero sizes, assign through a temporary pointer and only overwrite the original pointer on success.
functions.TIFFRawStripSize64: Returns the raw byte size of a strip. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and strip index. If the strip byte count is 0, it reports an error and returns `(uint64_t)-1`; otherwise it returns the byte count.
functions.TIFFFindField: Looks up a TIFF tag’s field descriptor in `tif->tif_fields`, optionally matching `TIFFDataType` (`TIFF_ANY` accepts any type). Use it to query metadata for a tag. Returns cached result if it matches, `NULL` if no fields or not found.
functions.TIFFDefaultTileSize: `TIFFDefaultTileSize` asks the TIFF codec to fill in default tile width/height. Call it with a valid `TIFF*` and two `uint32_t*` outputs; it writes suggested tile sizes via `tif_deftilesize`. Behavior depends on the codec/plugin attached to `tif`.
functions.TIFFCreateDirectory: `TIFFCreateDirectory` initializes a new in-memory TIFF directory by resetting the current directory state (`diroff`, `nextdiroff`, offsets, row/strip markers) after `TIFFDefaultDirectory()`. Use it to start a fresh directory; it always returns `0`.
functions.TIFFWriteRawStrip:
`TIFFWriteRawStrip` writes a strip’s raw encoded bytes directly. Use it only after write setup, passing a valid strip index and byte count. It returns bytes written or -1 on error; it rejects invalid strips and can’t grow separate-plane images by strips.
Yes, this is API misuse. TIFFWriteRawStrip expects the caller to supply a valid strip index for the current image layout. Before calling it, fully initialize the TIFF directory with consistent tags such as IMAGEWIDTH, IMAGELENGTH, SAMPLESPERPIXEL, BITSPERSAMPLE, PLANARCONFIG, and ROWSPERSTRIP, then compute or validate the strip number with TIFFNumberOfStrips() or TIFFComputeStrip(). Only pass strip values in the range [0, TIFFNumberOfStrips(tif)-1]. Do not use arbitrary fuzz-derived 32-bit strip indices. Also ensure the byte count matches the raw uncompressed data expected for that strip and check the return value for -1 on failure.
functions.TIFFRGBAImageOK: `TIFFRGBAImageOK` checks whether a TIFF can be read as RGBA and, if not, writes a reason to `emsg`. Call it before RGBA decoding; it returns 1 if supported, 0 on unsupported bit depth, float samples, missing decoder, etc.
functions._TIFFcalloc: `_TIFFcalloc` is libtiff’s wrapper for zero-initialized allocation. Use it like `calloc(nmemb, siz)` for TIFF internals. If either `nmemb` or `siz` is 0, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it calls `calloc` and returns the allocated block or `NULL` on failure.
functions.TIFFWriteEncodedTile: `TIFFWriteEncodedTile` writes one tile’s encoded data to a TIFF. Use it only on write-capable tiled images, with a valid `tile` index and `data/cc` for the tile payload. It checks bounds/buffer setup, reserves write buffer, and returns `-1` on error.
functions.LogLuv24toXYZ: Decodes a 24-bit LogLuv pixel into CIE XYZ. Use `XYZ[3]` as output. It extracts luminance and chroma; if luminance is nonpositive, returns `(0,0,0)`. If chroma decode fails, it falls back to neutral `u,v` before converting.
functions.TIFFSwabLong8: `TIFFSwabLong8` byte-swaps a 64-bit integer in place (endianness conversion). Pass a valid `uint64_t*`; it reverses all 8 bytes. Used when TIFF data endianness differs from host. If already same-endian, swapping would corrupt the value.
functions.TIFFUnlinkDirectory: `TIFFUnlinkDirectory` removes the `dirn`-th directory from a TIFF chain by patching the previous directory’s next-pointer. Use it only on writable files; it returns 0 and reports an error on `O_RDONLY`. It walks the directory list, with classic TIFF vs BigTIFF offsets handled separately.
functions.TIFFFlushData: `TIFFFlushData` flushes pending write data for a TIFF being written. Use it after writing/encoding to force buffered data out. If not in write mode, it returns 1. If `TIFF_POSTENCODE` is set, it runs `tif_postencode` first; failure returns 0.
